title: NULL, error handling and input validation
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its C rules.
Trace the example and identify data or control flow.
Recognize common failure and safety cases.
Apply the concept in a tested C program.

understand.concept: NULL is a null pointer constant commonly used to represent an absent pointer. Error handling defines how a function reports invalid input, failed allocation, failed I/O or another exceptional condition. Validation checks assumptions before using values or resources.
understand.whyItMatters: A program becomes more predictable when failures are explicit and callers know whether an operation succeeded.
understand.analogy: Treat each resource and operation as having a clear contract, valid lifetime and failure path.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace the C standard, compiler or library specifications.

explain.narrative:
NULL is a null pointer constant commonly used to represent an absent pointer. Error handling defines how a function reports invalid input, failed allocation, failed I/O or another exceptional condition. Validation checks assumptions before using values or resources.

Check object bounds, lifetimes, arithmetic limits and all relevant return values. Compile with warnings enabled and test both normal and failure paths.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: The function rejects a null output pointer, a non-positive total and a part outside the permitted range. It writes the result only after validating the inputs.

practise.guidedTask: Identify every invalid input and explain why the function returns false.
practise.independentTask: Design a function with a documented error result and tests for null pointers, zero values and out-of-range inputs.
hints: Validate external input at the boundary where it enters the program.
A NULL check alone does not prove a non-null pointer is valid.
Do not silently replace invalid input with a plausible default unless the interface contract says to do so.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable way to protect correctness?
options: Validate preconditions, bounds and failure results.
Ignore the type and lifetime rules.
questions.answer: Validate preconditions, bounds and failure results.
questions.explanation: C requires explicit handling of object validity and operation failures.

questions.prompt: How should the example be checked?

Ignore diagnostics and test only once.
questions.answer: Compile with warnings and test expected and failure cases.
questions.explanation: Warnings and targeted tests provide evidence for correctness.
